Subject: Next step: sizing kickoff for dedicated pool

Hi Sasha / Amy,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really helpful to understand Aurora's latency targets and the mix of sync (patient-facing) vs async (batch) workloads. Per our discovery, I recommend we lock a 60-minute sizing call next week to bring in Marcus (solutions engineering) and walk through:

- Observed qps and P95 latency targets by endpoint
- Tokenization and average/peak sequence lengths
- KV/prefix cache expectations and acceptable cold-starts
- Initial replication/availability and regional placement (we discussed east/west)

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue 6/16 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00
- Wed 6/17 09:00–10:00 or 15:00–16:00

If none of these work, drop a couple windows and we’ll accommodate. I attached the kickoff agenda and a short example CSV schema for the load profile if you want to pre-share numbers.

Goal for the call: produce a rough dedicated pool sizing + recommended autoscale/burst plan so procurement can scope costs.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
(415) 555-0129

Attachments:
- Redwood-Kickoff-Agenda.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
- Aurora_DMP_Load_Profile.csv (csv, 48KB)

Hi Sean — thanks for the recap. Wed 6/17 15:00–16:00 PST (that’s 18:00–19:00 here) would work best for our platform team. Amy is out Tue but can make Wed.

A couple quick notes before the call so Marcus can have context:
- Baseline qps today: ~12 sustained; peak ~85 (10min rolling) during morning influx
- Typical seq len median ~120 tokens; 95th ~520 tokens for longer notes
- We’ll want replication across us-west-2 and us-east-1, but prefer primary in west
- We plan to keep PHI in our VPC; the call can include architecture constraints

I’ll upload a trimmed sample of our traffic to the CSV and share ahead of time.

Thanks,
Sasha

Aurora Health

Thanks for the context, Sasha — helpful. I pulled together a short pre-read so we can hit the ground running on Wed:

Highlights I want to cover on the call (15–20 min each):
- Quick recap of latency/availability SLOs and mapping to pool config
- Expected GPU vCPU/memory footprints per model variant (a few scenarios based on seq len)
- Batching/throughput trade-offs and recommended queue sizing for burst 85 qps
- KV cache sizing and estimated warm-up behaviors

If you can drop the sample CSV into the Calendly invite or share the Drive link that’d be ideal. I’ll bring a couple sizing scenarios: small (single replica, high-QPS optimized), medium (2–3 replica baseline + autoscale), and a high-availability plan with cross-region replicas.

Agenda note: can we allocate the first 10 minutes for Aurora’s security constraints (VPC/KMS) so we don’t bury that later? If so, I’ll make sure we include Priyom for any compliance questions.
